definition: A system design in which ongoing human feedback (ratings, corrections, preferences) is continually collected and used to improve a deployed AI system over time.
details: Human feedback loops are used both during model training (as in RLHF) and in production systems, where user interactions and corrections can inform future model updates or fine-tuning.

explainer.lead: A human feedback loop continually collects ratings, corrections, and preferences and feeds them back to improve a deployed AI system. It matters because it lets a live system keep improving from real usage rather than staying fixed at launch.

tiers.eli5: Every time users correct the system or say they liked an answer, that feedback is saved and used to make the system better next time.
tiers.practitioner: Teams collect feedback during training, as in RLHF, and in production, where user interactions inform future updates or fine-tuning. A pitfall is that feedback can be sparse, noisy, or biased, so it must be curated before it shapes the model.
tiers.paperLevel: A system design in which ongoing human feedback, such as ratings, corrections, or preferences, is continually collected and used to improve a deployed AI system over time; it is used both in training and in production.

explainer.example: A deployed assistant logs thumbs-up and thumbs-down signals, and the highest-quality corrected responses are later used to fine-tune the next model version.
